what_happened: The operator had queued jobs A4–A9 to depend on a rejected A3 job id. The operator then said that lowering A4 and A5 to low priority would hold them back. It didn't: drain dispatched A4 next anyway, because priority only affects ordering, not whether a job is eligible. The operator used the kill switch, closed A4 and A6–A9, and re-asked them depending on the replacement ids as0j and 18fc.
cause: Dependencies are bound to a job id, and the plan reads any terminal state of that id as met rather than as landed and verified. A rejected and re-asked job leaves the old id terminal with nothing linking it to its replacement. The operator's workaround was also unsafe: priority is not a hold, and Athena gave the operator no way to hold a dependent job or to see that the dependency was wrongly counted as satisfied.
prevention: Two changes together. (1) When a job is re-asked or rejected, record a successor link from the old id to the new id. Treat a dependency as met only when the job it resolves to, following successor links, is landed and verified. A rejected id with no landed successor leaves its dependents blocked. (2) Add an explicit hold state for queued items that drain never dispatches, so no one has to use priority as a hold. At queue time, show each dependency's resolved state and refuse to queue against a rejected id.
proposed_request: Make queue dependencies resolve to landed work. When a job is rejected and re-asked, record the new job id as the old id's successor. Drain and the plan treat a dependency as met only when the job it resolves to, following successors, has landed and been verified. A dependency on a rejected job with no landed successor keeps its dependents blocked. When an item is queued, report each dependency's resolved state, and refuse a dependency on a rejected id that has no successor. Add a hold state for queued items that drain never dispatches, and a command to place and release it. Acceptance: a test where A3 is rejected and re-asked, and A4 depends on A3's old id, shows A4 is not dispatched until the new A3 lands; a test shows a held item is never dispatched whatever its priority; a test shows priority alone does not make a blocked item eligible.
